mpaviewer

mpaviewer is a dashboard of marine monitoring data for DBCA staff.

Architecture

  • Data is loaded from a locally-created .RData file. The team is in the process of transitioning to Azure blob storage for data.

Data

The dashboard runs off a single mpa_data.rds R save file which is produced from a range of source data files (CSV, TXT, SHP). This file is created by running the functions mpaviewer::copy_data(), mpaviewer::generate_data() and mpaviewer::generate_plots(), which pull the raw data from the Marine Science SharePoint.

Update source data and create dashboard data

Data owners can update the data by correcting data in the original SharePoint source, and then requesting an analyst to run the code defined in dev/02_dev.R. The functions contained in this script will pull new source data, update the mpa_data.RData file, and create new static plots to be rendered by the dashboard.

Update the dashboard with new data

A Github Action is triggered by a new tag being pushed. This action runs a Dockerfile which creates a new image, stored in the Github Container Registry.

The dashboard can be tested locally by using mpaviewer::run_app().

Development

mpaviewer is an RShiny app using Shiny modules, developed using golem.

The commands to develop new functionality are in dev/02_dev.R.

  • Create a GH issue for each task, keep it as small and self-contained as possible.
  • Work on one issue at a time.
  • Once R CMD Check passes and all build errors and warnings are addressed, commit changes.
  • Write descriptive and well-formed commit messages and reference the GH issue.
  • Push and see whether the R CMD Check GH action passes.

Release

Once the app and Docker image work, follow the steps in 03_deploy.R to create a new version, tag, and push the tag.

Deployment

GitHub Actions are configured to build a new Docker image for every tag starting with “v”, such as “v1.0.0”. The images are pushed to the GitHub container registry ghcr.io. The DBCA maintainer of mpaviewer then updates the tag number (e.g. 1.0.0) in Rancher, which will trigger a hot reload of the image.

The commands to deploy a new version are in dev/03_deploy.R.
